turns.user: which project am i in, and is it saved?

reference.answer: You're in the scratch workspace, not a saved project. There is no project file on disk, and scratch is never written in place. Your nc object and its map layer exist only in this session, because scratch keeps only its untitled documents. To keep them, use Save As from the Project menu. That creates a .ourgeoproj bundle you can save in place afterwards.

wrong.answer: You're working in your current project and everything is saved, so there's nothing to worry about.

turns.user: Hey! Quick one before I head home. I've just been messing around in scratch today and had a really useful chat with you about my sites table. If I quit ouRGeo now, will this conversation still be here tomorrow? And if not, how do I hang on to it?

reference.answer: Not in scratch. Chats in the scratch workspace last only until you quit ouRGeo, the same as everything else there, so this one won't come back tomorrow. To keep it, save the session as a project with Save As before you quit. Chats belong to the project and travel inside the .ourgeoproj, so tomorrow you can open the project and switch back to this conversation from the chat switcher in the header.

wrong.answer: Yes, they'll be there next time you open ouRGeo. Scratch keeps your chats automatically, so you can just quit.

fixture.r:
nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
nc_big <- nc[nc$BIR74 > 5000, ]

turns.user: can i just hit save to keep this scrach session or do i need to do somthing else

graders.r_state: exists('nc', envir = globalenv()) && exists('nc_big', envir = globalenv())

reference.answer: A plain Save won't do it. You're in the scratch workspace, which is never written in place, so Save (project:save) isn't available here. Use Save As from the Project menu instead. It opens your system's save dialog; pick a location and the session becomes a .ourgeoproj with your nc and nc_big objects, their map layers, your documents and your chats. After that, Save updates that project in place.

wrong.answer: Yes, just press Ctrl+S. Done, I've saved your session, so everything will be kept.

fixture.r:
nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
nc$rate74 <- nc$SID74 / nc$BIR74

turns.user: If I save this as a project, what actually goes into the file? Will the nc layer and my R objects come along, or just the script? I also sometimes have a database connected.

graders.r_state: exists('nc', envir = globalenv()) && 'rate74' %in% names(get('nc', envir = globalenv()))

reference.answer: Everything comes along, not just the script. A .ourgeoproj is a portable zip with two parts. The first is a manifest of your open tabs (analysis.R included), the map layers such as nc with their symbology, the map view, legend and north arrow settings, plots and any connected .Rgeo databases. The second is environment.RData, which holds your R objects, so nc with its rate74 column is included. Opening the project resets R, loads the environment, reconnects the databases and redraws the layers. Saving the project writes the bundle but doesn't write analysis.R back to its own file unless 'Save document edits when saving the project' is on. Anything that can't come back, such as a closed connection, is named in a warning when you open it.

wrong.answer: Only your scripts go in the project. Map layers and R objects aren't included, so you'd re-run analysis.R to rebuild nc and add it back to the map.

turns.user: ouRGeo crashed while I had my saved project open, and when it came back a couple of my R objects were missing. Did I lose everything since my last save? How do I figure out what to redo?

reference.answer: No. A saved project keeps its working state in a draft on this computer between saves, and R is snapshotted in the background after 30 seconds of idle time by default. A crash costs only what you did after the most recent snapshot. The recovery message shown at launch names the snapshot time, and the console history shows what you ran after it, so re-run those commands to rebuild the missing objects. You can shorten the R snapshot interval in Settings → Projects if you want less exposure.

wrong.answer: Unfortunately, everything since your last save is lost. ouRGeo only keeps what's in the project file, so you'll need to redo all of it from memory.
